tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

schema.description:

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

A workflow size guideline is configured for this session: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,
  perform and verify the operation, then disable it in a `finally` block. If
  background control still cannot work, report that limitation instead of
  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or
  a cross-frame JS walker.
- The normal local flow attaches to the running Chrome/Chromium CDP endpoint. No browser ids or local profile selection.

## plugin:desktop-commander:desktop-commander
Desktop Commander provides tools for working with the user's authorized device.
- Filesystem tools handle direct file and directory operations within configured access boundaries.
- Terminal process tools support shell commands, REPLs, and long-running processes. start_process creates a process session; interact_with_process sends input; read_process_output reads later output; force_terminate ends a session.
- Search tools are session-based. start_search creates a search session; get_more_search_results reads its results; stop_search ends it early.
- Absolute paths are generally the most reliable because relative paths depend on the active working directory.
- allowedDirectories and each tool's schema, annotations, and documented constraints define the operational boundaries.

# Claude Code mods

Function-hook plugins ("Claude Mods"), built 2026-10-02 from the session audit
(`/watch` of Chase AI's "Claude Mods" video + a read of the last 30 transcripts).
Synced to both machines through the `~/.claude` repo.

| Mod | Event | Shows | Usage |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo-band` | `turn.complete`, timer | Band: `repos: 3 dirty · 1 unpushed`, **Closeout** / **Closeout + exit** buttons; `/repos` lists them | none (local git) |
| `next-steps` | `session.start`, `turn.complete` | Band: 3 buttons. At start, newest `docs/handoffs/*.md`; after a turn, Haiku's suggestions. A press fills the prompt box to edit; Enter sends. `/next-steps off\|on` | one Haiku call per answered turn |
| `job-watch` | `session.start`, 10-min timer, task notifications | Status line: scheduled jobs, `errors.log`, recall eval; toasts when a job runs or a background task finishes; `/jobs` | none |
| `merge-cleanup` | after a `gh pr merge` Bash/PowerShell call | Toast naming the branches/worktrees removed (verified merged only; see `feedback_post-merge-cleanup`) | none |
| `where` | after Write/Edit/NotebookEdit | `/where [filter]` pane of recent files with copy-path buttons | none |
| `twin-copy-guard` | around Write/Edit/NotebookEdit, `turn.complete` | At turn end, names a hook/skill twin left unpatched (`~/.claude/hooks` ↔ `~/.codex/hooks`, `~/.claude/skills` ↔ `~/.agents/skills`) and offers **Copy across** when the pair matched before the edit; `/twins` lists every differing pair | none |
| `config-encoding-guard` | `session.start`, after Write/Edit/Bash/PowerShell, `turn.complete` | Catches a UTF-8 BOM or CP1252 garbling (`â€”`, `â–“`) in `~/.claude`/`~/.codex` config (see `project_settings-json-bom-trap`); offers a repair that keeps `.encoding-bak` and never writes JSON that will not parse; `/encoding` | none |
| `slate-status` | `session.start`, 30-min timer | Status line: `slate: DUE · 1/5 active · 2 to do` from `project-triage/portfolio.py slate-check`; toasts when it changes and is not OK; `/slate` lists problems | none |
| `pm` | `/pm` | Opens the live project board (`project-triage/board.py --background`): reuses the one running on this machine, else starts it tied to this session. The shell's `pm` runs the same command. | none |
| `progress-line` | after TaskCreate/TaskUpdate/TodoWrite (main loop only), 1 s timer (8/s while an agent runs) | Thin band, stacked above the other bands: `━━━━╸──── 4/7  ⠹ Explore  ✓ 1  3m12s`; `✓ all done` for 5 s, then hides. `/progress-clear` clears a stuck line | none |
| `landed` | `session.start` (background scan) | `/landed [today\|week\|N] [refresh] [project]`: files created or changed, grouped by project, both machines, from `project-triage/landed.py` | none |

Added 2026-10-03 (from the Nate Herk mods video + a 45-day transcript audit):
`repo-band` now fetches every repo once at session start, shows `↓N` behind, and
before Claude's first edit in a repo each session fetches it and asks **Pull first /
Edit anyway / Cancel** when it is behind origin. `job-watch` now shows `milvus ✓/✗`
(Docker-hosted Milvus for memsearch) and toasts when it goes down; machines with no
milvus container show nothing.

Windows note: on this machine `~/.codex/hooks` is not a mirror (1 file), and 6 of the
skills in `~/.claude/skills` are junctions into `~/.agents/skills` (same file, never
flagged). The other ~42 are real copies, so twin drift there is real (`harvest`
differed on 2026-10-03).

## Loading

**The folder is the list.** Every folder here with `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` loads on both
machines, unless it has a `.disabled` file or fails `claude plugin validate`. Nothing is
hand-listed (set 2026-10-03; before that the list lived in three places and drifted).

- `mods-sync.ps1` (Windows) sets the user env var `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS`.
- `mods-sync.sh` (Mac) writes `~/.claude/mods/.loadlist` (gitignored); `~/.zshrc` reads it:
  ```sh
  [ -f ~/.claude/mods/.loadlist ] && export CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS="$(cat ~/.claude/mods/.loadlist)"
  ```
- `dev-sync` and `closeout` run the sync and report one line:
  `mods: 8 loaded, 1 disabled, 0 invalid`. A broken mod is named and left out, never loaded.
- Turn one off on both machines: `touch ~/.claude/mods/<name>/.disabled`, commit, sync.
  Turn it back on: delete the file.
- A changed list takes effect after a restart of Claude Code (and a new shell on the Mac).

Headless `claude -p` runs report "hooks modules are turned off ... rollout switch
served off" (seen 2026-10-02); the mods are for interactive sessions.

## Checking

```sh
claude plugin validate ~/.claude/mods/<mod>
claude plugin test ~/.claude/mods/<mod>     # needs the rollout switch on
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# mods-sync.sh (Mac): load every mod in ~/.claude/mods, nothing hand-listed.
#
# Same rules as mods-sync.ps1: a mod loads when it has .claude-plugin/plugin.json, has no
# .disabled file, and passes `claude plugin validate`. The list is written to
# ~/.claude/mods/.loadlist (gitignored, per machine), which ~/.zshrc reads:
#
#   [ -f ~/.claude/mods/.loadlist ] && export CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS="$(cat ~/.claude/mods/.loadlist)"
#
#   bash ~/.claude/mods/mods-sync.sh              # validate and write .loadlist
#   bash ~/.claude/mods/mods-sync.sh --no-validate
# no `set -u`: macOS bash 3.2 errors on empty arrays under it
root="$HOME/.claude/mods"
validate=1; [ "${1:-}" = "--no-validate" ] && validate=0
loaded=(); disabled=(); invalid=()
for dir in "$root"/*/; do
  dir="${dir%/}"; name="$(basename "$dir")"
  [ -f "$dir/.claude-plugin/plugin.json" ] || continue
  if [ -e "$dir/.disabled" ]; then disabled+=("$name"); continue; fi
  if [ $validate -eq 1 ] && ! claude plugin validate "$dir" >/dev/null 2>&1; then invalid+=("$name"); continue; fi
  loaded+=("$dir")
done

value="$(IFS=:; echo "${loaded[*]:-}")"
before="$(cat "$root/.loadlist" 2>/dev/null || true)"
[ "$before" != "$value" ] && printf '%s' "$value" > "$root/.loadlist"

line="mods: ${#loaded[@]} loaded, ${#disabled[@]} disabled, ${#invalid[@]} invalid"
[ ${#disabled[@]} -gt 0 ] && line="$line | disabled: $(IFS=,; echo "${disabled[*]}")"
[ ${#invalid[@]} -gt 0 ] && line="$line | INVALID (not loaded; run claude plugin validate): $(IFS=,; echo "${invalid[*]}")"
[ "$before" != "$value" ] && line="$line | changed: open a new shell and restart Claude Code"
echo "$line"

"""One-time settings.json change from the 2026-10-31 mod review.

Turns off context-mode, browser-use (synced) and desktop-commander (synced),
and removes the context-mode-cache-heal SessionStart hook. Text edits only, so
the file's formatting is kept. Writes nothing unless every edit matches and the
result parses as JSON. Backup: settings.json.bak-2026-10-31.
"""
import json, pathlib, shutil

p = pathlib.Path.home() / ".claude/settings.json"
s = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

edits = [
    ('    "context-mode@context-mode": true,', '    "context-mode@context-mode": false,'),

assert "context-mode-cache-heal" not in s

shutil.copy2(p, p.with_name("settings.json.bak-2026-10-31"))

content.text:
Your mods were not the main thing slowing sessions down. A plugin called `context-mode` was.

**What slows you down**
- `context-mode` adds about 0.5 s to every Bash call. You made about 27,000 Bash calls in 30 days.
- It also adds about 0.3 s to most other tools and to every prompt.
- But Claude used its own tools for only 0.6% of all tool calls.
- Two more plugins come from your claude.ai account sync. They start a server each session. `browser-use` had 0 calls in 30 days. `desktop-commander` had 8.

**What I did to your mods**
- I found a bug. Line 44 of `~/.zshrc` listed only 5 mods by name. So 6 of your 11 mods never loaded on this Mac, including `progress-line`, which you built on 10-29.
- I fixed that line. It now reads `~/.claude/mods/.loadlist`, as the mods README says.
- I turned off 5 mods:
  - `next-steps`: it made a Haiku call after every turn, and I found no sign you use it. (Mod button presses may not show in the logs, so my count may be low.)
  - `slate-status` and `landed`: they ran background scans, and I found no sign you use them.
  - `config-encoding-guard`: it guarded against a Windows-only problem. The off switch syncs, so it is now off on the laptop too. Undo: `rm ~/.claude/mods/config-encoding-guard/.disabled`.
  - `twin-copy-guard`: on this Mac the hook and skill "twins" are links to the same file, so it had nothing to guard.
- 6 mods stay on: `repo-band`, `job-watch`, `merge-cleanup`, `where`, `pm`, `progress-line`.
- I kept your startup hooks. Each one takes less than 0.7 s, and they run at the same time.
- I committed and pushed this in `~/.claude` (`56acdd6`, `e4d1243`). The full numbers are in `~/.claude/HARNESS_FIXES.md`.

**What I did not do**
- Your rules block Claude from editing `settings.json`, so I did not touch it. I checked that it is unchanged and still valid.
- To turn off the 3 plugins, I wrote a script. I tested it on a copy, and only the intended lines changed.

**What you do now**
1. Run: `! python3 ~/.claude/jobs/4e4af1e8/tmp/apply-settings.py` (it backs up the file first). If you delete this job before you run it, the script goes with it. The manual steps are in the "Open" section of `~/.claude/HARNESS_FIXES.md`.
2. Open a new terminal window.
3. Restart Claude Code.

To turn a mod back on: `rm ~/.claude/mods/<name>/.disabled`, then run `bash ~/.claude/mods/mods-sync.sh` and restart.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/closeout

# Closeout

One command for the end-of-day sequence: day log → loose ends → memory → STATUS and handoff → commit and push → one verdict.

Step 0 asks Eric one question at most. After his answer (or when Step 0 is skipped), run every
other step without pausing: invoking closeout authorizes the whole sequence. Commit and push is
standing-authorized for every DEV repo (each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine ends with it, and
unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other). On Windows or in Cowork,
read [`PLATFORMS.md`](PLATFORMS.md) for the commands that differ.

**Scope.** Every DEV repo with uncommitted or unpushed work (touched this session or not), plus
`~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory`.
A repo whose `CLAUDE.md` says its data stays local (DexaProject is the precedent) is committed,
not pushed, and listed.

**Clear to sign off when** the closing `where-was-i.py --sweep` (step 4) shows no `ACTION` line
except repos listed under "Still open" with their reason, no background job is still writing,
`.errors.log` is empty or its entries are reported, and every repo touched today has a STATUS entry
dated today with a concrete first `## Next` item, and every `card-check` gap is fixed. Questions
only Eric can answer (a receiver nobody named, a decision recorded under `## Open questions`) do
not block: `/startup` shows them tomorrow; list them under "Still open" and say "Clear to sign off".
Anything short of that: "Not clear", naming the one thing blocking.

If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and
note it. A risky fix goes under "Still open".

## Step 0 — Day log (once a day)

Closeout is the one end-of-day step Eric keeps, so it carries the two inputs the biweekly
`status-report` trusts: the supervisor log and the shipped ledger. Before 2026-10-31 they lived
only in `interview-me` and `harvest`, and both lapsed (last log 09-14, last ledger row 10-06).

`{vault_status_log}` is `vault_status_log` in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`.
When `{vault_status_log}/<today>.md` or `{vault_status_log}/.asked-<today>` exists, today's log is
already taken (usually by `interview-me`): leave out the three Part 0 questions and keep only
question 4, and only when step 1 finds a candidate. No candidate and no Front Burner question
(step 2 below) as well: skip this step.

0. **Front Burner checks** (plan `project-triage/docs/plans/2026-10-31-front-burner-self-maintaining.md`):
   run `python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py dates` and `... drift`. Resolve every line you
   can from evidence (STATUS dates, commits) with a cited `add-update` note. Every remaining line
   whose `needs_eric` is true (`--json`) becomes one more numbered question in step 2's batch:
   overdue step or no date → "done, new date, or no hard date?"; `off_board` → "start X?";
   `quiet` → "keep X or park it?". Ask every one, not just the first. Record answers the same day:
   one command per answer, `python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py decide X <action>`:
   done → `done --step N`; new date for an overdue step → `redate --step N --date YYYY-MM-DD`;
   a date for a row that has none (`no_date`) → `redate --date YYYY-MM-DD` (no `--step`: it adds one); no hard date →
   `no-date [--step N] --reason "..." --source "..."`; an old "no hard date" still true →
   `confirm-no-date`; a row with a dated step and an old record → `drop-no-date` (no question
   needed); keep a quiet row → `keep-quiet`; "no,
   leave it off the board" → `keep-off` (stores the exact moment, so only later work is asked
   about). Start or park with `set-status`. Do not hand-edit these fields. Skipped lines are not
   blocking: list them under "Still open".

1. **Ship candidates.** Read today's dated `## Current state` lines in every repo touched today
   (the sweep in Step 1 lists them; `landed.py show --days 1` also works). A candidate is work
   handed to a person or put in use: sent, delivered, shared, presented, merged for a user, live.
   Drop any project that already has a row dated today in the ledger (`{vault_output_ledger}`).
2. **Ask once**, all at once, short answers accepted: the three Part 0 questions from
   `interview-me/SKILL.md` (that file holds their wording; left out when today's log is taken), plus:
   > 4. Did anything ship or go to someone today? I found: <candidates, or "nothing">.

   then 5, 6, ... : one per Front Burner `needs_eric` line from step 0.
3. **Write the log** (only when you asked the Part 0 questions) exactly as `interview-me` Part 0 says (output format, honest-zero rule,
   append to an existing file). On an honest zero, write the empty marker
   `{vault_status_log}/.asked-<today>` instead, so the next closeout today skips the ask.
4. **Each confirmed ship:** run the `harvest` skill for it. Eric's yes is the ship evidence harvest
   Step 1 needs; the ledger row is the required part, lesson articles only when harvest finds them.

**Done when** the log file or the marker exists for today and every confirmed ship has a ledger
row dated today.

## Step 1 — Sweep

- **Repo sweep:** `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --sweep` (~4 s). It checks every git
  repo under `DEV/` (two levels) and the three config repos, and prints one line per repo needing
  attention; exit 1 means at least one `ACTION`. Another session, harness or machine may have left
  that work; name each such repo in the report. Flags:
  - `DIRTY`, `UNPUSHED`, `NO-UPSTREAM`, `BRANCH-AHEAD:<b>`, `BRANCH-UNPUSHED:<b>` (a local branch
    holding commits on no remote), `WORKTREE-DIRTY:<path>`: work not on GitHub. Step 4 pushes it.
  - `NOT-A-REPO`: a `.git` folder git cannot use, so the folder's work is tracked nowhere. List it;
    repair is project work, not closeout. It blocks only if this session wrote files there.
  - Info, never blocking: `STASH:<n>` (list it; leave the stash alone), `NO-REMOTE`, `DETACHED`
    (a pinned checkout), `LIVE` (session files the hooks rewrite every turn; the daily backup
    pushes them).
- **Background jobs** still running (shells, agents, workflows): wait for each to finish, or name
  it as the blocker. A job that writes after the push leaves work unpushed.
- **Registry drift:** `python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py crosswalk` (`portfolio_json` is
  in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.macos.json`). It only reports. List every item under "Still
  open", any folder created this session first (a project started without a row). Fixing waits
  for a project session. `drive_unreachable` means the Drive checks never ran: say so.
- Unfinished tasks from this session (TaskList), and anything promised to Eric this session and
  not delivered.

## Step 2 — Memory

Memory capture failing silently is Eric's top recurring worry; this step runs every time.

- **`~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log`:** surface every entry, fix the hook issue if
  obvious, then archive and clear it as in claude-stack-doctor's `FIXES.md` → Memory pipeline
  (append to `.errors-ledger.log`, then `cp /dev/null`). The file is tracked in `global-memory`,
  so this happens before step 4's push.
- **Today's transcript** `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` exists and changed within
  the last few hours.
- **New durable decision or active thread:** update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md`
  (2,500-char cap; consolidate first) or write a Tier A memory with the `memory-write` skill.
- **Tier A stays on this machine** (its slug is built from the absolute path, which differs per
  machine). Every durable, project-scoped Tier A fact written today also goes into the repo:
  `docs/STATUS.md` for current state, `docs/DECISIONS.md` for a decision and its reason, the dated
  handoff for detail.

## Step 3 — STATUS, handoff, cards

**Handoff**, when real work happened (not just Q&A): `<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md`;
workspace or system work with no single repo goes to `~/DEV/docs/handoffs/`
(`~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` is read-only history). Plain markdown that Codex,
Antigravity or a fresh Claude session can resume from:
- what was worked on and why
- decisions made, with the reasoning that would be lost
- exact paths of every file created or modified
- next actions, most important first
- anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)
- suggested skills: which ones the next session should invoke, by name

Link, don't copy: if a spec, plan, ADR, issue or commit already holds the detail, give its
path, URL or sha. Redact keys, passwords and personal data; the note is pushed to GitHub.

**`docs/STATUS.md`, in every repo touched, every time.** The next session reads it first, on
either machine, in any harness. Rewrite these sections in place, short:
- `## Current state`: two to five lines on where things stand today.
- `## Next`: most important first. Item 1 is one concrete action (a command to run or a file to
  open); `~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py` shows it to Eric the next morning.
- `## Open questions`: each decision waiting on Eric as its own top-level bullet, the question and
  enough context to answer it without opening another file. `/startup` lists this section across
  repos, so write the question itself, never a pointer. Mark answered items `ANSWERED <date>: …`
  or strike them (`~~…~~`). Leave the section empty when nothing waits.
- `## Gotchas`: anything that will bite the next session.

Over 20 KB, or more than 15 dated entries under `## Current state`: first move entries older than
14 days and finished `## Next` items, verbatim, to the end of
`docs/handoffs/STATUS-archive-<YYYY>-Q<n>.md`. The archive is a search root; entries move, they
are never deleted.

Then:
1. `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --decisions --days 1` prints what tomorrow's
   `/startup` shows as "Decisions waiting on you". Every decision left open today appears there as
   a readable question; fix the repo's `## Open questions` until it does.
2. `python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/landed.py scan --days 1` (~1 min), then
   `python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py card-check`. Fix every gap with
   [`CARDS.md`](CARDS.md), then re-run `card-check`.
3. `bash ~/.claude/scripts/harvest-dev-docs.sh`: copies every repo's `docs/*.md` into
   `~/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs/` (gitignored, indexed by memsearch). One line of output.
4. **Deliverables:** a finished file made for someone else today (PDF, deck, report, sheet) gets a
   copy in Drive `03_REPORTS`, uploaded through the API (writes through the `_DRIVE` mount hang):
   `cd <file's folder> && gws drive +upload ./<file> --parent 18lZZ4ep4pmK6upQfEcTUuLNlDdSAk5Au --name YYYY-MM-DD_<Sport>_<Topic>_<Type>_<Audience>.<ext>`.
   The repo keeps the source. Health data stays local.
5. **Front Burner phone page** (after Step 0's answers are recorded): render
   `python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py today --html <dir of portfolio_json>/outputs/front-burner.html`
   (allow-listed fields only: cleared names, fixed step labels, dates; it refuses an unsafe name).
   Then (1) `Artifact read` the `meta.artifact_url` in `portfolio.json` and confirm the header says
   **private**; if it is shared or unreadable, do not publish there: publish to a new artifact,
   put its URL in `meta.artifact_url`, and tell Eric once; (2) publish the file to that `url`;
   (3) `Artifact read` it again and confirm the header says **private** (owner only). If that read
   fails or shows it shared, the publish is not done: tell Eric at once that the page may be
   exposed, list it first under "Still open", and the verdict is "Not clear" until he has checked
   the page's Share menu. Needs a Claude session (Codex skips this step).
   A project row started today without `phone_ok` shows as "Project #n" until the `project`
   skill's name check clears it.

## Step 4 — Commit and push

- **Registry edits first, alone.** In project-triage, if `git status --porcelain portfolio.json`
  shows a change, commit that file alone as `data: board edits <YYYY-MM-DD>`. The board's "N
  unpushed registry edits" counts these; folded into another commit, they become a JSON merge
  conflict when the other machine edits too.
- **Before staging,** read the files about to be added (`git status --porcelain`). Anything the
  `BLOCKED` list in `~/.claude/hooks/session-autopush.js` names (`.env`, keys, credentials,
  secrets, token files, databases, DEXA) or over 50 MB stays out: add it to `.gitignore`, or leave
  it unstaged and list it. Health data never reaches GitHub.
- Every repo in scope: stage, commit with a descriptive message, `git pull --no-rebase`, push. On
  a merge conflict follow `dev-sync/SKILL.md` Step 3.3 (the one home for conflict steps), push, and
  list the file under "Still open". A side branch the sweep flagged: `git push -u origin <branch>`.
- `~/.claude/mods` changed this session: `bash ~/.claude/mods/mods-sync.sh`; list any invalid mod.
- **`global-memory` is pushed every time,** even on a light session: it is the only repo that
  carries memory to the other machine, and the nightly backup is too late for a same-day switch.
- Nothing to commit: one line, move on.
- **Prove it:** re-run `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --sweep`. Every `ACTION` line left
  is either fixed now or goes under "Still open" with its reason. A push that hangs is usually a
  credential prompt: look for `git credential-osxkeychain get` in `ps`; fix and retry once, as
  `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kristinarash-DEV/memory/project_brew-git-keychain-hang.md` says.
  Still hanging: "Not clear", that repo is the blocker.

## Step 5 — Verdict

`python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/landed.py show --days 1` lists every file that landed today (git in
every DEV repo, file times on Drive and in the vault), so the report names every created or
modified file with its full path. The ledger lives in `~/.claude/global-memory/landed/` and was
pushed in step 4.

```
## Closeout — <date>

**Day log:** written / honest zero / already taken today; **Shipped:** <ledger rows added, or "none">
**Committed & pushed:** <repos + one-line summary, or "nothing to commit">
**STATUS.md:** updated in <repos>
**Memory:** captured ✓ / issue found: <what> / skipped: <what> (Cowork)
**Handoff:** <path, or "not needed — no substantive work">
**Registry drift:** <N items, or "none">
**Still open:** <numbered list, or "none">

Clear to sign off. / Not clear: <the one thing blocking>.

**Landed:** <landed.py show output, grouped by project>
**Cards:** <card-check output after the step 3 fixes>
```

The block above the verdict line fits on one screen: Eric is leaving. Landed and Cards come last
because the next session picks up from them; trim both to projects with work today, keeping every
card that still has a gap.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/closeout

# Closeout

One command for the end-of-day sequence: day log → loose ends → memory → STATUS and handoff → commit and push → one verdict.

Step 0 asks Eric one question at most. After his answer (or when Step 0 is skipped), run every
other step without pausing: invoking closeout authorizes the whole sequence. Commit and push is
standing-authorized for every DEV repo (each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine ends with it, and
unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other). On Windows or in Cowork,
read [`PLATFORMS.md`](PLATFORMS.md) for the commands that differ.

**Scope.** Every DEV repo with uncommitted or unpushed work (touched this session or not), plus
`~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory`.
A repo whose `CLAUDE.md` says its data stays local (DexaProject is the precedent) is committed,
not pushed, and listed.

**Clear to sign off when** the closing `where-was-i.py --sweep` (step 4) shows no `ACTION` line
except repos listed under "Still open" with their reason, no background job is still writing,
`.errors.log` is empty or its entries are reported, and every repo touched today has a STATUS entry
dated today with a concrete first `## Next` item, and every `card-check` gap is fixed. Questions
only Eric can answer (a receiver nobody named, a decision recorded under `## Open questions`) do
not block: `/startup` shows them tomorrow; list them under "Still open" and say "Clear to sign off".
Anything short of that: "Not clear", naming the one thing blocking.

If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and
note it. A risky fix goes under "Still open".

## Step 0 — Day log (once a day)

Closeout is the one end-of-day step Eric keeps, so it carries the two inputs the biweekly
`status-report` trusts: the supervisor log and the shipped ledger. Before 2026-10-31 they lived
only in `interview-me` and `harvest`, and both lapsed (last log 09-14, last ledger row 10-06).

`{vault_status_log}` is `vault_status_log` in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`.
When `{vault_status_log}/<today>.md` or `{vault_status_log}/.asked-<today>` exists, today's log is
already taken (usually by `interview-me`): leave out the three Part 0 questions and keep only
question 4, and only when step 1 finds a candidate. No candidate and no Front Burner question
(step 2 below) as well: skip this step.

0. **Front Burner checks** (plan `project-triage/docs/plans/2026-10-31-front-burner-self-maintaining.md`):
   run `python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py dates` and `... drift`. Resolve every line you
   can from evidence (STATUS dates, commits) with a cited `add-update` note. Every remaining line
   whose `needs_eric` is true (`--json`) becomes one more numbered question in step 2's batch:
   overdue step or no date → "done, new date, or no hard date?"; `off_board` → "start X?";
   `quiet` → "keep X or park it?". Ask every one, not just the first. Record answers the same day:
   one command per answer, `python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py decide X <action>`:
   done → `done --step N`; new date for an overdue step → `redate --step N --date YYYY-MM-DD`;
   a date for a row that has none (`no_date`) → `redate --date YYYY-MM-DD` (no `--step`: it adds one); no hard date →
   `no-date [--step N] --reason "..." --source "..."`; an old "no hard date" still true →
   `confirm-no-date`; a row with a dated step and an old record → `drop-no-date` (no question
   needed); keep a quiet row → `keep-quiet`; "no,
   leave it off the board" → `keep-off` (stores the exact moment, so only later work is asked
   about). Start or park with `set-status`. Do not hand-edit these fields. Skipped lines are not
   blocking: list them under "Still open".

1. **Ship candidates.** Read today's dated `## Current state` lines in every repo touched today
   (the sweep in Step 1 lists them; `landed.py show --days 1` also works). A candidate is work
   handed to a person or put in use: sent, delivered, shared, presented, merged for a user, live.
   Drop any project that already has a row dated today in the ledger (`{vault_output_ledger}`).
2. **Ask once**, all at once, short answers accepted: the three Part 0 questions from
   `interview-me/SKILL.md` (that file holds their wording; left out when today's log is taken), plus:
   > 4. Did anything ship or go to someone today? I found: <candidates, or "nothing">.

   then 5, 6, ... : one per Front Burner `needs_eric` line from step 0.
3. **Write the log** (only when you asked the Part 0 questions) exactly as `interview-me` Part 0 says (output format, honest-zero rule,
   append to an existing file). On an honest zero, write the empty marker
   `{vault_status_log}/.asked-<today>` instead, so the next closeout today skips the ask.
4. **Each confirmed ship:** run the `harvest` skill for it. Eric's yes is the ship evidence harvest
   Step 1 needs; the ledger row is the required part, lesson articles only when harvest finds them.

**Done when** the log file or the marker exists for today and every confirmed ship has a ledger
row dated today.

## Step 1 — Sweep

- **Repo sweep:** `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --sweep` (~4 s). It checks every git
  repo under `DEV/` (two levels) and the three config repos, and prints one line per repo needing
  attention; exit 1 means at least one `ACTION`. Another session, harness or machine may have left
  that work; name each such repo in the report. Flags:
  - `DIRTY`, `UNPUSHED`, `NO-UPSTREAM`, `BRANCH-AHEAD:<b>`, `BRANCH-UNPUSHED:<b>` (a local branch
    holding commits on no remote), `WORKTREE-DIRTY:<path>`: work not on GitHub. Step 4 pushes it.
  - `NOT-A-REPO`: a `.git` folder git cannot use, so the folder's work is tracked nowhere. List it;
    repair is project work, not closeout. It blocks only if this session wrote files there.
  - Info, never blocking: `STASH:<n>` (list it; leave the stash alone), `NO-REMOTE`, `DETACHED`
    (a pinned checkout), `LIVE` (session files the hooks rewrite every turn; the daily backup
    pushes them).
- **Background jobs** still running (shells, agents, workflows): wait for each to finish, or name
  it as the blocker. A job that writes after the push leaves work unpushed.
- **Registry drift:** `python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py crosswalk` (`portfolio_json` is
  in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.macos.json`). It only reports. List every item under "Still
  open", any folder created this session first (a project started without a row). Fixing waits
  for a project session. `drive_unreachable` means the Drive checks never ran: say so.
- Unfinished tasks from this session (TaskList), and anything promised to Eric this session and
  not delivered.

## Step 2 — Memory

Memory capture failing silently is Eric's top recurring worry; this step runs every time.

- **`~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log`:** surface every entry, fix the hook issue if
  obvious, then archive and clear it as in claude-stack-doctor's `FIXES.md` → Memory pipeline
  (append to `.errors-ledger.log`, then `cp /dev/null`). The file is tracked in `global-memory`,
  so this happens before step 4's push.
- **Today's transcript** `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` exists and changed within
  the last few hours.
- **New durable decision or active thread:** update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md`
  (2,500-char cap; consolidate first) or write a Tier A memory with the `memory-write` skill.
- **Tier A stays on this machine** (its slug is built from the absolute path, which differs per
  machine). Every durable, project-scoped Tier A fact written today also goes into the repo:
  `docs/STATUS.md` for current state, `docs/DECISIONS.md` for a decision and its reason, the dated
  handoff for detail.

## Step 3 — STATUS, handoff, cards

**Handoff**, when real work happened (not just Q&A): `<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md`;
workspace or system work with no single repo goes to `~/DEV/docs/handoffs/`
(`~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` is read-only history). Plain markdown that Codex,
Antigravity or a fresh Claude session can resume from:
- what was worked on and why
- decisions made, with the reasoning that would be lost
- exact paths of every file created or modified
- next actions, most important first
- anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)
- suggested skills: which ones the next session should invoke, by name

Link, don't copy: if a spec, plan, ADR, issue or commit already holds the detail, give its
path, URL or sha. Redact keys, passwords and personal data; the note is pushed to GitHub.

**`docs/STATUS.md`, in every repo touched, every time.** The next session reads it first, on
either machine, in any harness. Rewrite these sections in place, short:
- `## Current state`: two to five lines on where things stand today.
- `## Next`: most important first. Item 1 is one concrete action (a command to run or a file to
  open); `~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py` shows it to Eric the next morning.
- `## Open questions`: each decision waiting on Eric as its own top-level bullet, the question and
  enough context to answer it without opening another file. `/startup` lists this section across
  repos, so write the question itself, never a pointer. Mark answered items `ANSWERED <date>: …`
  or strike them (`~~…~~`). Leave the section empty when nothing waits.
- `## Gotchas`: anything that will bite the next session.

Over 20 KB, or more than 15 dated entries under `## Current state`: first move entries older than
14 days and finished `## Next` items, verbatim, to the end of
`docs/handoffs/STATUS-archive-<YYYY>-Q<n>.md`. The archive is a search root; entries move, they
are never deleted.

Then:
1. `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --decisions --days 1` prints what tomorrow's
   `/startup` shows as "Decisions waiting on you". Every decision left open today appears there as
   a readable question; fix the repo's `## Open questions` until it does.
2. `python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/landed.py scan --days 1` (~1 min), then
   `python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py card-check`. Fix every gap with
   [`CARDS.md`](CARDS.md), then re-run `card-check`.
3. `bash ~/.claude/scripts/harvest-dev-docs.sh`: copies every repo's `docs/*.md` into
   `~/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs/` (gitignored, indexed by memsearch). One line of output.
4. **Deliverables:** a finished file made for someone else today (PDF, deck, report, sheet) gets a
   copy in Drive `03_REPORTS`, uploaded through the API (writes through the `_DRIVE` mount hang):
   `cd <file's folder> && gws drive +upload ./<file> --parent 18lZZ4ep4pmK6upQfEcTUuLNlDdSAk5Au --name YYYY-MM-DD_<Sport>_<Topic>_<Type>_<Audience>.<ext>`.
   The repo keeps the source. Health data stays local.
5. **Front Burner phone page** (after Step 0's answers are recorded): render
   `python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py today --html <dir of portfolio_json>/outputs/front-burner.html`
   (allow-listed fields only: cleared names, fixed step labels, dates; it refuses an unsafe name).
   Then (1) `Artifact read` the `meta.artifact_url` in `portfolio.json` and confirm the header says
   **private**; if it is shared or unreadable, do not publish there: publish to a new artifact,
   put its URL in `meta.artifact_url`, and tell Eric once; (2) publish the file to that `url`;
   (3) `Artifact read` it again and confirm the header says **private** (owner only). If that read
   fails or shows it shared, the publish is not done: tell Eric at once that the page may be
   exposed, list it first under "Still open", and the verdict is "Not clear" until he has checked
   the page's Share menu. Needs a Claude session (Codex skips this step).
   A project row started today without `phone_ok` shows as "Project #n" until the `project`
   skill's name check clears it.

## Step 4 — Commit and push

- **Registry edits first, alone.** In project-triage, if `git status --porcelain portfolio.json`
  shows a change, commit that file alone as `data: board edits <YYYY-MM-DD>`. The board's "N
  unpushed registry edits" counts these; folded into another commit, they become a JSON merge
  conflict when the other machine edits too.
